params.place: on the map: the Strait of Malacca between Malaysia and Sumatra, Singapore at its narrow end

moments.what: tankers sail in a line up the strait
STRAIT OF MALACCA writes along the water
a red barrier slams down across the narrow end
the map dims to night and the barrier's lamps glow
the tankers bunch up behind the barrier
the camera pulls back over the islands
question marks pop over the sea routes south

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The Strait of Malacca closes overnight. Which way do the oil tankers go now?

params.place: on the map: the Phillip Channel at Singapore, the narrowest point

moments.what: a thought bubble frames the map
the bubble's dots float up
the camera pushes in on the strait
the water lane glows thin between the coasts
Malaysia traces in light
the islands across the channel glow
Sumatra traces in light
the measuring bar starts drawing across the channel
the bar locks in and the width stamps on its sign
a tanker squeezes between the bar's ends

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It's only a thought experiment, but look how thin this lane is: between Malaysia and the island of Sumatra, just 2.8 km wide at its narrowest.

params.place: on the map: the Andaman Sea entrance of the strait, tankers queuing in

moments.what: the camera pulls back to the strait's northern mouth
a day counter sign lights up
barrels start stacking on the leading tanker's deck
tankers start streaming in
barrels stack up on a tanker deck with the figure
the tankers squeeze into the lane
a drop of oil glints on the deck
a pie dial on a buoy fills to the share
the leading tanker slips into the narrow lane
ships all over the sea light up
a dashed oil trail runs along the whole lane

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And yet every day about 23.2M barrels of oil squeeze through it, 29% of all the oil that moves by sea.

params.place: on the map: from the Gulf across the Indian Ocean, through the strait to East Asia

moments.what: a ruler draws along the whole strait
the length stamps on the ruler
the camera pulls back to all of Asia
an oil rig rises on the Gulf
GULF writes beside it
China lights up with a factory
Japan lights up with a factory
Korea lights up and a route joins them all through the strait

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It runs 900 km from end to end, the short cut from the oil fields of the Gulf to the factories of China, Japan and Korea.

params.place: on the map: the strait being rubbed out, the coasts closing up

moments.what: an eraser sweeps across the strait
the lane disappears into land
a tanker sails in from the west
a FROM INDIA sign pops on the tanker's wake
the tanker bumps into the new land and stops
Sumatra flashes
Malaysia flashes

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Now rub it out. A tanker sailing east from India meets a wall of land, with Sumatra on one side and Malaysia on the other.

params.place: on the map: the Sunda Strait between Sumatra and Java

moments.what: a question mark hops along Sumatra's coast
a door outline opens at the south end
SUNDA STRAIT writes in the gap
the gap glows
Sumatra traces
Java traces
a new dashed route draws south round Sumatra into the gap

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So where's the next door? The Sunda Strait, a gap between Sumatra and Java, far to the south.

params.place: on the map: the Lombok Strait east of Bali, then up past Borneo

moments.what: a second tanker peels off further east
its route draws on along Java
LOMBOK STRAIT writes in the gap
Bali lights up beside it
the route turns north
Borneo lights up as the route runs past it

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Other tankers sail further still, through the Lombok Strait, east of Bali, and then north past Borneo.

params.place: on the map: Singapore at the tip of the Malay Peninsula

moments.what: the camera swings back north
Singapore glows red, its border traced
cranes and a container ship appear at its harbour
the closed lane beside it darkens
the harbour lights flicker
a NO WAY THROUGH sign drops at the harbour mouth
the container ship turns back

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Stranger still, Singapore, a port city at the narrow end of the lane, suddenly sits beside a blocked lane with no way through.

params.place: on the map: the whole of Asia, every ship route bending round Indonesia

moments.what: the closed lane flashes red
container ships line up behind it
crates start stacking on the quay
the share stamps on the crate stack
the camera pulls back to the whole region
the container ships sound their horns and turn
every ship route turns south
each ship's bow swings south onto the new routes
the routes stretch round the islands
the long loop closes past Borneo

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Because this one lane carries about 25% of all the goods the world trades, every one of those ships now takes the long way round.

params.place: on the map: back at the Strait of Malacca

moments.what: MALACCA pin pops on the strait
HORMUZ pin pops far to the west
both pins pulse red
a comment bubble pops between them
the camera glides back to the strait
the tankers sail back into the lane
the strait comes back into frame, tankers sailing up the lane
